input: It should be noted that the position with regard to the delayed package has deteriorated, in that the package now stands 4 weeks behind the date to which the supplier originally committed, and the underlying cause of this slippage lies with the supplier itself: fabrication capacity at the supplier's works was committed elsewhere first, and the package was rescheduled behind other work that was already in the shop. The consequences of this delay are not confined to the package, because the equipment contained in the package is erected before the piping tie-ins that follow on from it, and those tie-ins in turn release the loop checks and the pre-commissioning activities that sit behind them, so a slip at this particular point tends to move every dependent activity in the sequence. Against that background, the mitigation that is being proposed is essentially one of resequencing: installation fronts that do not depend on the delayed package would be brought forward, and the crews released by the slip would be held on those fronts rather than being stood down. The project board owns the mitigation and will settle the resequenced order, and the EPC schedule is being reissued on the same basis. What resequencing cannot do, however, is recover the erection window itself, and the balance of the delay that remains after mitigation is still under discussion with the supplier, whose revised date the board has not yet accepted
target:
The delayed package now stands 4 weeks behind the supplier's committed date, and the cause sits with the supplier: fabrication capacity was committed elsewhere first, and the package was rescheduled behind work already in the shop. The delay lands on the installation sequence at its most constrained point. The equipment in the package is erected before the piping tie-ins that follow it, and the tie-ins release the loop checks and the pre-commissioning work behind them, so a slip at the package moves every activity that hangs from it.

The mitigation proposed is resequencing. Installation fronts that do not depend on the delayed package are brought forward, and the crews released by the slip are held on those fronts rather than stood down. The project board owns the mitigation and settles the resequenced order. The EPC schedule is reissued on the same basis, with the package carried at the supplier's revised date and the brought-forward fronts in their new order. Resequencing recovers crew time and protects the later fronts; it does not recover the erection window itself, and the balance of the delay that survives mitigation is still under discussion with the supplier, whose revised date the board has not yet accepted
